idiom_name: plain objects/attributes in a list; __getattr__ forwarding for transparent delegation
implementation_notes: Python needs no component interface: duck typing accepts any object with the expected method, so the entity is a class holding a components list (or explicit attributes) and the update loop calls the hook it needs - the classic container and slots are just composition. When the container should also expose a component's members as its own, __getattr__ forwards lookups after normal attribute access fails (docs.python.org: it is called when the default lookup raises AttributeError), which replaces hand-written delegating methods but hides the indirection from readers and tooling - so use it deliberately and delegate to a named component, read via self.__dict__ to avoid recursion. For large entity populations, esper provides the data-oriented form: integer entity ids, plain classes or dataclasses as components, and Processor classes as the systems.
pitfalls: __getattr__ runs only after normal lookup fails, so a component member is silently shadowed by any same-named entity attribute; special methods are looked up on the type, so delegation never covers them.
Duck typing gives no required-component guarantee: entity.physics.update(dt) raises AttributeError on the first frame that needs it, long after assembly - validate the component set in the assembler.
Mutating the components list while iterating it skips or repeats components; build a new list or apply changes after the pass.
